picks.title: First harmonised standard supporting the AI Act published in the Official Journal
picks.excerpt: The European Commission published the reference to the first harmonised standard supporting AI Act implementation in the Official Journal of the EU, a milestone ahead of the application of high-risk AI system requirements; further harmonised standards are expected to follow.
picks.rationale: Primary EU document: the first harmonised standard referenced in the Official Journal gives builders of high-risk AI systems a presumption of conformity under the AI Act, which makes it the most practical compliance news of the day. It is a distinct event from the 10-15 AI Office incident-enforcement card. No og:image, so media needs an in-article or EU asset.

picks.title: Taiwan targets illicit AI server exports to China with five-year prison terms
picks.excerpt: Taiwan is moving to criminalize unauthorized exports of AI servers and chips to China with up to five years in prison, following a US tariff deal and a Super Micro smuggling raid, which could make it easier to charge AI chip smugglers.
picks.rationale: A new Taiwanese government move on AI-chip and server export controls, separate from the 10-02 US DOJ smuggling arrest and the 10-19 China draft catalogue. The domain is off-list (an exception because no allowed outlet covered it), and the measure is not confirmed as a proposal or as cabinet-approved, so the copy must call it a move or proposal unless enrichment confirms approval.

picks.title: AI sovereignty: preserving UK agency in an AI-enabled world
picks.excerpt: A published advisory letter to the UK Minister for AI sets out how the UK can build the capability to make strategic choices about current and future AI technology, framed as preserving national agency.
picks.rationale: An official UK government publication on sovereign AI capability. It is a different event from the 10-15 GOV.UK AI-risk defences card. Describe it as an advisory letter to the minister, not as adopted policy. The og:image is the generic gov.uk banner.

picks.title: Daedalus: Greece unveils new supercomputer as it eyes role in Europe's AI race
picks.excerpt: Greece inaugurated Daedalus, a €58.9 million, 85.69-petaflop supercomputer in Lavrio ranked 31st worldwide, letting researchers and businesses train AI models on data kept within the country.
picks.rationale: A concrete sovereign-AI compute launch by a government: Greece inaugurated the machine, with figures for cost, petaflops and ranking, so researchers and businesses can train models on data kept in the country. It brings in a European national-strategy angle not covered in the 30-day history.

picks.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
picks.excerpt: Court filings in Character.AI's Chapter 11 case show Disney required the deal be consummated through bankruptcy, seeking a perpetual license via a '363 free and clear' order while Character.AI retains liability for chatbot child-safety lawsuits.
picks.rationale: A follow-up backed by new court filings. Character.AI's Chapter 11 filings show the structure: Disney would get a perpetual license through a '363 free and clear' sale order while the chatbot child-safety liability stays with Character.AI. That bears on AI liability law, and the card is about litigation, not M&A. Attribute the 'get out of lawsuits' framing to WIRED's reading of the filings.
